reason: The cited evidence confirms oxygen contamination up to >1 wt.% in powder-metallurgy HfNbTaTiZr and mentions defects like dislocations, but it provides no data on defect-induced electronic states, activation energies, or conductivity mechanisms. The key premises about specific defect energy levels and their impact on conductivity prediction accuracy are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Oxygen contamination introduces defect states and lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
These defect states have specific activation energies (~0.4–0.5 eV and ~1.1–1.2 eV) governing low- and high-temperature conduction.
Oxygen levels up to ~1 wt.% are achievable and relevant in powder-metallurgy HfNbTaTiZr.
Defect-inclusive modeling will reduce prediction error compared to perfect-crystal analytical models.
